tonight.headline: Waivers clear at 01:00 tonight and you are not claiming anything. That is the decision.
body: Week 2 has not kicked off. ESPN has KEI returns 118.1 to your 116.2 and gives you 49%. You start three Jaguars — Lawrence, Cam Little and the Jacksonville defense — in one game at Denver, down from four after you moved Golden into the flex at 17:50 today.

Priority here never resets and you are 5th of 10. The wire's best available player tonight is Jordan Mason, a lead back, and the recommendation is still not to claim him — the reasoning is below rather than left as an omission. The only thing that touches waivers is the Coker card, and it only fires if he clears unclaimed and shows as a free agent.

case.label: The quarterback question you will see in the app
case.body: ESPN's own numbers now prefer Stafford to Lawrence — 17.2 to 14.6 this week, QB13 to QB18 on the rank field. Lawrence stays in. Yahoo's Week 2 board has Lawrence QB11 and Stafford QB14, the open thesis on Lawrence has not tripped any of its conditions, and its falsification clause is 'Stafford clearly out-scores Lawrence in two consecutive weeks', which is one week from being testable. Sources genuinely disagree here and the side taken is Yahoo's, on the rushing floor: Lawrence added 359 rushing yards and 9 scores last season and Stafford, in Sports Illustrated's words, 'does not scramble ever.'

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Stafford out-scores Lawrence in Week 2 and again in Week 3, or Jacksonville name a change at quarterback. A single Monday-night Stafford game does not reopen it.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Before Sunday 11:00, Mexico City — Golden and Jackson both kick off then
doFirst.title: Send Team 13 the Golden-for-Lamar Jackson offer
doFirst.subtitle: Recomputed on tonight's file: +26.5 you, +12.2 them, identical to Sunday. Golden's usage went up today, which means the price does too.

case.label: Their slot column, read on this file
case.body: Josh Allen is at slot 0 and starting and is not being asked for. Lamar Jackson sits at slot 20, their bench, scoring them nothing every week in a one-quarterback league. Travis Kelce occupies their RB/WR/TE flex at 178.1 and Xavier Worthy sits behind him at 173.9. Golden's 190.3 walks straight into that flex ahead of both.

case.label: What you are giving, and it just got more expensive
case.body: PlayerProfiler's Week 1 usage report has Golden at 85.5% of snaps, an 88.4% route share and a 28.6% target share — 12 targets, 6 for 95 with Jordan Love throwing. That is the buy profile the strategy file describes, and selling it is the thing that file warns against. This offer survives that only because of what comes back.

case.label: Why it survives when the Chem sale did not
case.body: The same route-share logic killed the McLaurin sale in Chem this afternoon. The difference is direction: there you were giving the best-usage player and receiving a WR2. Here you give a WR3 in a room that already has Rashee Rice and Garrett Wilson, and receive the second-ranked quarterback on Yahoo's Week 2 board at the one position a ten-team wire cannot replace. Consolidating toward the best player in the deal is the standing rule, and you are on the right end of it.

case.label: Jackson's health, re-checked
case.body: 324 passing yards and two touchdowns in a 41-23 win in Week 1, and Yahoo have him QB2 for Week 2 against New Orleans with 220 passing and 55 rushing projected. No Week 2 injury reporting for him was retrievable today — every search returned 2025 material — so read that as 'nothing found', not 'confirmed healthy'.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Both totals reproduce to the decimal for the fourth run running — 2054.0 to 2080.5 and 1969.9 to 1982.1. The season field has not moved since it was published, so this is priced on a preseason opinion of Golden and of Jackson alike. On a one-week horizon it is worth 4.7 points; the case is the season, and the season is the number that has not updated.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 trade or drop a quarterback, acquire a third receiver, or start Worthy in the flex before answering. Or Golden posts a second double-digit-target game at the Jets — then his price is above this offer and it should be withdrawn rather than re-sent.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · check after 01:00 Wednesday · only if Coker reads FREE AGENT, never as a claim
doFirst.title: If Coker clears waivers unclaimed, add him for Kayshon Boutte
doFirst.subtitle: Unchanged from this morning and still correct: the only thing that ever stopped this was the priority cost, and a free agent has none.

case.label: Why this is a card and not a claim
case.body: The decline on record stands for tonight's waiver run: priority here never resets, you are 5th of 10, and Coker would not start over Rice, Wilson or Golden. But if no other manager claims him, an unclaimed waiver player becomes a free agent, and a free agent costs nothing in either league. The distinction is the whole card.

case.label: The player
case.body: 8 of 9 for 138 and two touchdowns in Week 1 — the top receiving line in the NFL that week — played mostly after he rolled the ankle. He called the Monday boot precautionary and expects to practise Wednesday; nothing has updated that since. He is being claimed in Chem tonight, where priority resets and it is free.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Boutte, 15.8% rostered: one catch on two targets, 46% of snaps, third receiver behind Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson. Added 9 September, so the seven-day churn window closes before waivers clear. No thesis was ever recorded for him.

case.label: The likely outcome
case.body: Coker is 51.0% rostered and his ownership is rising faster than anything else on this wire, +0.30 on the day. Expect a rival to claim him and this card to expire quietly. That is a fine outcome; it costs nothing to have written it down.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Coker is limited or absent in Carolina's Wednesday practice report — then leave Boutte alone. Or Boutte's snap share passes Hutchinson's this week. Or a rival claims Coker, which simply retires the card.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · decide on Friday's designation · the drop locks when Las Vegas kick off, Sunday 14:05
doFirst.title: Keep Michael Mayer until Bowers's Friday designation
doFirst.subtitle: Nothing today moved this. Las Vegas need Bowers through multiple consecutive practices before they clear him, and the first one is Wednesday.

case.label: What today's reporting actually says
case.body: RotoWire, relaying Schefter: there is 'a realistic chance' Bowers sits only Week 1, and the Raiders' medical staff will require him to practise on multiple consecutive days before clearing him for the Chargers on 20 September. Wednesday is the first of those days. No practice report exists yet, so Friday is the earliest this is answerable.

case.label: The contradiction in your own log
case.body: The decision log currently holds two entries about this player pointing opposite ways: an open HOLD saying the modal return is Week 3, and a closed WRONG saying the thesis was falsified because Bowers returns in Week 2. Both cannot be live. This card supersedes them: the answer is genuinely unknown until Friday and the log is being reconciled to say so.

case.label: Why Mayer is worth the seat for four more days
case.body: IPADE's flex takes a tight end, which Chem's does not, so a startable second tight end has real value here. If Bowers sits again, Mayer starts for Las Vegas and is playable in your flex. The seat he occupies has no competing claim on it tonight.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Bowers practises in full Wednesday or carries no designation Friday — then Mayer is the drop before Las Vegas kick off. If Bowers is limited or sits, keep Mayer through Week 2 and read it again next Monday.

whatWentWrong.title: This morning's brief listed an unresearched wire back as a limitation. Here he is.
whatWentWrong.lead: Jordan Mason: 15 carries, 59 yards, a touchdown and four red-zone carries in Week 1, 67.6% rostered, and ESPN flags him QUESTIONABLE on nothing anyone is reporting.

case.label: What he is
case.body: Minnesota's lead back by a margin: 15 carries to Aaron Jones's 12 in Week 1, and four of the backfield's red-zone carries. DraftKings Network read him as 'a strong FLEX or a solid RB2' against Chicago, who finished 27th in rushing yards allowed and 26th in EPA per rush last season and gave up 125 on 22 attempts in Week 1.

case.label: The designation nobody can source
case.body: The league file carries him QUESTIONABLE. No injury appears anywhere in today's reporting on him — the 14 September outlook piece discusses his Week 2 role and does not mention one. Treat the tag as stale rather than meaningful, and note that this is a read, not a clearance.

case.label: Why the answer is still no
case.body: He would be your third running back behind Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley, and the flex is Golden's. Priority here never resets and the standing rule is that it is spent only on a player who starts immediately or wins a league. A bench back, however good, is not that.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Taylor or Barkley misses time, or the Golden trade lands and the flex opens. Either makes Mason a starter, and a starter is what the priority is for.

whatWentWrong.title: The Golden-for-Lamar case had it backwards on which usage you should keep
whatWentWrong.lead: Golden's route share is the reason to want him. The offer goes out anyway — but for the return, not because he is expendable.

case.label: The number
case.body: 85.5% snap share, 88.4% route share, 28.6% target share, 12 targets (PlayerProfiler). This morning's card called Golden's usage a reason the offer was 'more costly to give' and then sent it at the same price. That is the right observation attached to the wrong conclusion about price.

case.label: Why it still goes
case.body: Because the return is a top-two weekly quarterback in a one-QB league and your receiver room already starts Rice and Wilson. The justification is consolidation, not that Golden is replaceable. Stating it the other way round is how an offer gets re-sent later at a worse price without anyone noticing the price changed.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Golden clears ten targets again at the Jets. At that point the honest move is to withdraw the offer rather than repeat it, and the falsification clause on the trade already says so.

case.label: The structural surplus
case.body: Team 13 roster two of the top three quarterbacks on Yahoo's Week 2 board — Allen at 1 and Jackson at 2 — in a league that starts one. Their flex is a 37-year-old tight end at 178.1 and their bench receiver is Worthy at 173.9. This is the shape the strategy file says to trade into: a team paying for nothing at one position and thin at another.

case.label: What it does to your lineup
case.body: Jackson replaces Lawrence at quarterback (312.9 for 282.0) and Tuten returns to the flex at 205.2 for Golden's 190.3. On the week it is worth 4.7 points at quarterback alone. Lawrence then becomes the trade chip rather than the starter, which also retires the Lawrence-Stafford argument.

case.label: The one-week horizon, stated plainly
case.body: Only weekly and full-season projections are published, and the full-season field has not moved across four snapshots. This offer clears the bar on a number that was set before the season and has not been updated since. On a rest-of-season market it might well look different; that market is not available here.

case.label: The risk
case.body: You are trading the highest route share on your roster. If Golden is a WR2 by Week 5 this looks like selling usage, which is the error the Chem brief just corrected in the other direction. The defence is that quarterback is the one slot a ten-team wire cannot refill and receiver is the one it can.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: They trade or drop a quarterback, acquire a third receiver, or start Worthy in the flex before answering. Or Golden posts a second double-digit-target game — then withdraw rather than re-send.

trades.sources: PlayerProfiler · Yahoo Sports · NFL.com · ESPN league file
trades.copyText: Hi — would you do Matthew Golden for Lamar Jackson? You're starting Josh Allen, so Jackson scores you nothing on the bench all season, and Golden goes straight into your flex ahead of Kelce (190.3 to 178.1). He ran an 88.4% route share with 12 targets in Week 1. On ESPN's season field it's about +12.2 for you — more than it is for me on this week's numbers. Happy to talk shape if you'd rather build it differently.

worthALook.name: Jordan Mason
worthALook.lead: The best player on this wire and the one you are deliberately not claiming. 15 carries, 59 yards, a touchdown and four red-zone carries in Week 1.

case.label: The role
case.body: Minnesota's lead back: 15 carries to Aaron Jones's 12, no targets, and four of the team's red-zone carries. DraftKings Network read him as a strong flex or solid RB2 against a Chicago run defense that finished 27th in rushing yards allowed and 26th in EPA per rush last season and gave up 125 on 22 carries in Week 1.

case.label: The designation to discount
case.body: ESPN lists him QUESTIONABLE. No injury appears in any reporting retrieved today, including a 14 September piece written specifically about his Week 2 outlook. Read the tag as stale; that is a judgement, not a clearance.

case.label: The price
case.body: A claim here spends priority that never resets, from 5th of 10, for the whole season. The standing rule is that priority goes to a player who starts immediately or wins a league. Mason would be your RB3 behind Taylor and Barkley with the flex already spoken for.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Taylor or Barkley misses time, or the Golden trade lands and opens the flex, or Mason posts a second week above 18 points while still unrostered here. Any of those makes him a starter, and a starter is what the priority is for.

worthALook.name: Ravens D/ST
worthALook.lead: 89.8% rostered nationally and free here, which is the largest ownership anomaly on this wire. Still not worth priority.

case.label: Why they look good
case.body: Under new coordinator Jesse Minter, Baltimore sacked Daniel Jones twice, forced an interception and held Indianapolis to 149 net passing yards in Week 1. Draft Sharks has them 4th for Week 2 at 8.4 projected and Sportsnaut has them 6th, hosting a New Orleans offense that was inconsistent in its opener.

case.label: Why the answer is hold
case.body: Your incumbent is 8th on the same Sportsnaut board after five sacks and two takeaways, and Denver missed 28 tackles on Monday night. The gap is a few projected points across one week, and it would cost a priority position you cannot get back. This is being claimed in Chem, where a claim is free, and declined here, where it is not — the asymmetry is the point.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Jacksonville finish outside the top 20 defenses in Week 2, or Baltimore are still free after tonight's waivers run and can be added as a free agent at no priority cost.

doNotChase.name: Cairo Santos
doNotChase.lead: The required kicker comparison, and it comes back hold.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Yahoo's Week 2 board has Cam Little 3rd. The best kicker on this wire is Will Reichard at 5th, then Chase McLaughlin 6th, then Cairo Santos 14th. Nothing available here outranks the kicker you already start, and Little returned 12.0 in Week 1.

case.label: And the seat is radioactive
case.body: This slot went Little to Boswell on 8 September and Boswell back to Little on 10 September. The decision log carries that pair twice as CHURN — once for the reversal and once for being right about it by luck. A third move in eight days on a kicker would be the tell the strategy file's review questions ask you to look for.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Little finishes outside the top 20 kickers across Weeks 2–4, or Jacksonville's implied team total drops below 18 for two straight weeks.

doNotChase.name: Jakobi Meyers
doNotChase.lead: A listed starting receiver at 79% rostered — a genuine anomaly, and still the wrong use of a priority you only get once.

case.label: What he is
case.body: Jacksonville's depth chart lists three starting receivers — Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr. and Jakobi Meyers — with Travis Hunter as a starting cornerback and only a package on offense. The role is real and the ownership number says a manager here blundered.

case.label: The number that kills it for this roster
case.body: He projects 9.5 this week and 182.4 on the season, behind Rice, Wilson and Golden, so he arrives as a bench receiver. Spending never-resetting priority on a bench receiver is the one thing the strategy file rules out by name, and it is the same reasoning that declined Coker as a claim here this morning. Being consistent about that is worth more than the player.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: He clears waivers unclaimed and becomes a free agent, at which point he costs nothing and Boutte is the obvious drop — behind Coker in that queue, not ahead of him.

cannotSee.label: Priority is one shot and its future value is unknowable
cannotSee.body: Every decline on this page — Mason, Meyers, the Ravens — rests on saving a waiver position for a player who has not appeared yet. There is no way to price that option. If nobody better arrives by Week 10, holding it will have been wrong and this brief will have been consistently wrong about it.

cannotSee.label: Whether unclaimed players become free agents here
cannotSee.body: The Coker card assumes an unclaimed waiver player reverts to free agency after processing. Every wire row in this snapshot reads WAIVERS with the same 07:00 UTC clearsAt and there are no free agents at all, so the setting cannot be confirmed from the file. Check the wire after 01:00 before acting.

cannotSee.label: Rival claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own pending claims. Coker is the fastest-rising player on this wire at +0.30 owned and you cannot see who else is queuing for him.

cannotSee.label: Season projections have not moved in four snapshots
cannotSee.body: Your optimal season total recomputes to 2054.0 exactly, for the fourth run running, and the trade recomputes to +26.5 / +12.2 to the decimal. Either the field updates on a schedule that has not fired yet, or it is a preseason artifact and every trade on this page is priced on August.

cannotSee.label: Six of fourteen matchup tiles are dashed
cannotSee.body: Denver, Kansas City, Indianapolis and the two Jacksonville tiles were researched today. Tennessee, Green Bay, Minnesota, the Jets and the Chargers were not, and are flagged rather than guessed.

cannotSee.label: Three starters are in one game
cannotSee.body: Lawrence, Cam Little and the Jacksonville defense all play at Denver at 14:05 Sunday. The projections treat them as independent and they are not — a Jacksonville blowout loss takes all three down together. There is no way to express that correlation in this data.
